faqs.question: What is Ayurveda?
faqs.answer: Ayurveda believes in a holistic approach to well-being that takes into account the harmony of the body, mind, and soul. Herbal therapies, dietary modifications, yoga, meditation, and lifestyle adjustments are frequently used as treatments in Ayurveda.

faqs.question: What is the main aim of Ayurveda?
faqs.answer: Ayurveda is based on the three life forces, known as doshas in the human body. They are known as pitta dosha, kapha dosha, and vata dosha. Each individual inherits a different combination of the three doshas. However, one is often more dominant than the others. An imbalance in the doshas leads to illness and health problems. Promoting health and preventing illness is the primary objective of Ayurveda.

faqs.question: Why should one practice the Ayurveda lifestyle?
faqs.answer: Ayurveda offers individualized advice based on a person's dosha (constitution type), acknowledging that every person is unique. This personalized care has the potential to improve wellness and health behaviors.

faqs.question: Can I learn Ayurveda if I am a beginner?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can learn Ayurveda if you are a beginner. It can be learned by anyone irrespective of age and experience.

faqs.question: What is the connection between Yoga & Ayurveda?
faqs.answer: Yoga and Ayurveda are both products of the old Vedic tradition, which offers a lot of intellectual, scientific, and spiritual knowledge. The goal of Ayurveda is to achieve internal equilibrium through herbal remedies, food habits, and lifestyle change and the goal of yoga is to perform asana, pranayama, and meditation to create physical and mental equilibrium. Together they offer a comprehensive approach to well-being.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Meditation & Yoga Nidra?
faqs.answer: Meditation is a practice that involves eliminating distractions to achieve a state of mental clarity, and heightened awareness. The aim is to reach a state of mindfulness and promote overall well-being.

faqs.question: What are the benefits of Yoga Nidra?
faqs.answer: Yoga Nidra is a guided process towards deep relaxation. It helps to eliminate sleep-related problems. It also helps to release suppressed emotions leading to greater emotional stability.

faqs.question: How do I start meditating?
faqs.answer: Set your intention for the meditation and start your practice. Try to start with a small duration (5-10 minutes) and you can increase the duration gradually. Firstly, find a quiet place with fewer distractions and get comfortable seated or lying down.

faqs.question: Is meditation better than asana practice?
faqs.answer: There is no such thing as meditation being better than asana practice. It all depends on the individual goals and needs. According to the eight limbs of yoga, meditation is one of the highest stages of yoga, and one must master the primary practices like asana and pranayama to reach the higher levels.

faqs.question: How different is Yin Yoga from other forms of Yoga?
faqs.answer: The majority of other yoga forms, such as Vinyasa, Ashtanga, or Hatha, use shorter holds between each position and more dynamic movement and transitions between them. They usually concentrate on improving cardiovascular health and increasing muscular strength and flexibility.

faqs.question: What is Yin Yoga good for?
faqs.answer: Yin yoga relieves the tension in the connective tissues. It aims to promote flexibility and circulation in the joints. It also develops a calm and peaceful inner being.

faqs.question: What is Yin Yang?
faqs.answer: Yin and Yang stand for the dual nature of everything in the cosmos. They are central ideas in Chinese philosophy. These ideas, which have their roots in Taoism, explain how seemingly incompatible or opposing forces are linked together and dependent upon one another in the natural world, giving rise to one another in the process.

faqs.question: Is Yin Yoga good for beginners?
faqs.answer: Yes, Yin Yoga is a great exercise for beginners. Yin yoga is a slow-paced yoga, which emphasizes relaxation, and mindful stretching.

faqs.question: Does this course have live classes?
faqs.answer: No, this course doesn't have live classes

faqs.question: Who needs Yin Yoga?
faqs.answer: Yin yoga is mainly good for stress relief, improving flexibility, and emotional balance, and relieving sleep issues.

faqs.question: Is Hatha good for beginners?
faqs.answer: Hatha yoga is a slow-paced yoga that is excellent for beginners. In Hatha Yoga, one generally practices static poses.

faqs.question: What is Hatha-style yoga?
faqs.answer: Hatha yoga focuses on mindfulness, breathing, and posture. All of the major upper and lower body muscle groups are targeted by the poses of hatha yoga.

faqs.question: Is Hatha yoga easy or hard?
faqs.answer: Hatha yoga is rather slow and mild, making it ideal for beginners or those who want a more relaxing yoga to hold yoga postures for a longer time.

faqs.question: Who should not do Hatha yoga?
faqs.answer: Women who are expecting or who have recently given birth shouldn't practice hatha yoga. Yoga can cause discomfort if you have any major joint issues or pain. So it is better one consults a doctor before engaging in the practice. Otherwise, everybody can practice hatha yoga irrespective of age and condition.

faqs.question: Can I do Hatha yoga at home?
faqs.answer: Yes, one can practice Hatha Yoga at home. It is easy to follow and slow-paced.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Ashtanga and Vinyasa yoga?
faqs.answer: Vinyasa yoga incorporates intense sequencing transitions between poses. It is recognized for its challenging positions, such as arm balances and inversions. The concept of vinyasa means to flow, by synchronizing the breath with the movement.

faqs.question: Is Ashtanga yoga the hardest?
faqs.answer: Due to its dynamic nature, Ashtanga Yoga is considered to be hard. Ashtanga Yoga has an asana sequence that is predetermined and needs to be learned in a precise order. And the continuous flow of the Ashtanga series can make the practice challenging.

faqs.question: Who should not do Ashtanga yoga?
faqs.answer: Anyone with high blood pressure, cardiac problems, or migraines should avoid the practice.

faqs.question: Is Ashtanga OK for beginners?
faqs.answer: Although Ashtanga can be challenging, the Ashtanga yoga primary series is a good place to start for beginners. It's a predetermined series of poses that you perform in a particular order to progressively increase your strength, flexibility, and concentration.

faqs.question: Is Hatha or Vinyasa better?
faqs.answer: Both types of yoga have their own benefits. Ashtanga Yoga has a sequence of poses predetermined. It is known for its continuous, flowing style of practice, in which one asana flows into the next without interruption. On the other hand, Hatha Yoga is slow-paced and has static poses.

faqs.question: What is the main philosophy of yoga?
faqs.answer: The philosophy of yoga believes that the mind, body, and soul are interconnected. It considers that spiritual ignorance is the root of all suffering. Integrating the body, mind, and soul and achieving positive goals to fight diseases of the modern world is the primary goal of yoga.

faqs.question: What are the eight limbs of yoga philosophy?
faqs.answer: The eight limbs of yoga are yama, niyama, asana, pranayama, pratyahara, dharana , dhyana, and samadhi.

faqs.question: Who is the founder of yoga?
faqs.answer: Maharishi Patanjali is considered the “Father of Yoga”. He has written 195 verses in the Patanjali Yoga Sutras which provides a structure for incorporating yoga into daily life. Lord Shiva on the other hand is also considered as the first yogi (Adiyogi) who imparted the knowledge of yoga to the immortal seven sages (Saptarishis).

faqs.question: Why is yoga philosophy important?
faqs.answer: Advocates of yoga argue that realizing one's own self is the first step toward achieving inner harmony. Yoga philosophy outlines a methodical procedure to do this. In order to achieve oneness with the Divine, yoga philosophy teaches moral principles, ethical standards, breathing exercises, and internal practices.

faqs.question: What do we learn in yoga philosophy?
faqs.answer: The philosophy of yoga offers an individual framework for maximizing the benefits of techniques including posture flow, breathing exercises, and meditation. And if one approaches yoga philosophically, then one gains control over their life.

faqs.question: What are the types of pranayama?
faqs.answer: There are different types of Pranayama. Some of the most common ones are Alternate Nostril Breathing, Abdominal Breathing, and Bee Breath.

faqs.question: What is pranayama and its importance?
faqs.answer: Pranayama helps our bodies release mental and physical blockages that hinder the flow of prana, or life force. Pranayama practiced consistently may strengthen the whole body. It also helps us to control the mind and prepare us for higher practices of yoga.

faqs.question: Which is the safest pranayama?
faqs.answer: Nadi Shodhana or Alternate Nostril Breathing is the safest pranayama.

faqs.question: Which time is best for pranayama?
faqs.answer: Practice pranayama either on an empty stomach in the morning or three to five hours after eating. You can practice calming pranayama right before bed. Practice pranayama before you meditate and after you complete your asana practice.

faqs.question: Can everyone practice pranayama?
faqs.answer: Anyone can practice pranayama and become aware of their breath. However, people with breathlessness, heart failure, or feeling tired while practicing pranayama may avoid and try savasana.

faqs.question: How to meditate for beginners?
faqs.answer: If you are a beginner you may choose a time and duration which is feasible (10-15 mins a day) and then gradually increase the time.

faqs.question: What exactly is meditation?
faqs.answer: We learn about ourselves and become our of our surroundings in meditation. It is a way of thinking and being that helps us live intentionally by highlighting the areas of our lives where we feel comfortable or trapped.

faqs.question: How many minutes to meditate?
faqs.answer: Different people have different meditation sessions with different durations. Research suggests it is beneficial to meditate for 40-45 minutes. If you're a beginner, begin with brief meditation sessions that last a few minutes, and as your meditation skills improve, add more time.

faqs.question: How to start meditating daily?
faqs.answer: To meditate daily one has to make it a habit. To get started, one may use guided meditation audio scripts or join a meditation/ yoga group where an instructor can guide him. Start small and set minimum durations to sit for meditations.

faqs.question: Which pose is best for meditation?
faqs.answer: Padmasana is one of the easiest and best poses to sit in meditation.

faqs.question: What happens during yoga nidra?
faqs.answer: Yoga Nidra involves lying down, to enter a deep state of conscious sleep, which leads to a profound level of awareness and relaxation.

faqs.question: What is the objective of yoga nidra?
faqs.answer: During Yoga Nidra, an instructor leads the exercise while the student is lying down in Savasana. The practice is combined with guided mental imagery to induce a deep level of relaxation in which the practitioner is still conscious of their surroundings.

faqs.question: How is yoga nidra different from meditation?
faqs.answer: Traditional meditation methods require a person to be in a seated posture, which aim to improve perception, intuition, and ability to focus attention and consciousness. Yoga Nidra is performed lying down, where awareness is present but the body is consciously asleep.

faqs.question: How long is yoga nidra?
faqs.answer: Yoga Nidra usually lasts between thirty and forty-five minutes.

faqs.question: Can we do yoga nidra daily?
faqs.answer: The yoga nidra calms the mind and promotes sleep by relaxing the body through mindful breathing exercises and guided meditation. Every day, 30 minutes of yoga nidra practice helps one to release tension and prepares the body for sleep.

faqs.question: What is the concept of mindfulness?
faqs.answer: Being mindful involves being aware of one's environment and inner states. By teaching people to observe their thoughts, feelings, and other in-the-moment sensations without judging or reacting.

faqs.question: How do I practice mindfulness?
faqs.answer: There are different techniques of mindfulness practices, such as walking meditation, eating meditation, mindful breathing, and others. One may try out different techniques in their day-to-day life to sustain their awareness of daily life.

faqs.question: Is yoga mindfulness?
faqs.answer: Yoga cannot exist without awareness and mindfulness. The goal of both yoga and mindfulness is to still the mind in order to develop a closer relationship with the self. Both of these direct us to become aware of breathing, by paying attention to our body's feelings and learning to accept reality as it is at any given time.

faqs.question: Is mindfulness a meditation?
faqs.answer: The practice of mindfulness requires one to keep attention or awareness of the present moment without judgment. Mindfulness practices consist of formal meditations to sustain awareness in daily life.

faqs.question: How do I start mindfulness?
faqs.answer: One can start their mindfulness journey by understanding the concept and the techniques of mindfulness practices. Thereafter after trying the different practices, one can start to incorporate the formal practices in their real life.

faqs.question: Why is office yoga important?
faqs.answer: Sitting for extended period of time which is common among office workers, may lead to musculoskeletal issues. These issues can be reduced with desk yoga.

faqs.question: How to do yoga at a desk?
faqs.answer: One can perform simple stretches sitting on the chair or standing using the table and wall. Individuals can also incorporate breaks to practice mindfulness to rejuvenate themselves from stress.

faqs.question: Is office yoga difficult?
faqs.answer: Office yoga is safe and easy to perform and can be performed by any individual of all ages. Office yoga provides support for the postures with the help of a chair, table, and wall.

faqs.question: How to improve posture at work?
faqs.answer: By performing stretches from time to time and being mindful of the sitting posture one may improve their posture. The right posture is to prevent your head from tilting and keeping your computer at eye level. Keep your back flat on the chair and pull your shoulders back. Avoid crossing your legs or ankles and place your feet flat on the ground. Straighten the upper back.

faqs.question: Is standing better than sitting?
faqs.answer: Both sitting and standing duration should be balanced. Reducing or breaking up the sitting time with standing or walking around will enhance blood circulation, metabolism, and mental well-being.

faqs.question: What is anatomy?
faqs.answer: Yoga anatomy gives us a knowledge of the fundamental workings of cells and the molecular processes of living things.

faqs.question: What is the relationship between yoga and anatomy?
faqs.answer: Understanding anatomy will make your yoga practice safer. It will help you to get a better knowledge of the correct posture for an asana and how it is beneficial for your body.

faqs.question: Why is anatomy and physiology important?
faqs.answer: It ensures the safe practice of yoga asana and pranayama as it gives an understanding of the functioning of the systems and the muscles and joints.

faqs.question: What is the basic physiology of yoga?
faqs.answer: Understanding how the body adjusts to yoga across bodily systems—including musculoskeletal, neurological, respiratory, cardiovascular, endocrine, reproductive, and digestive.
